data.title: Time Picker
data.tagline: Choose a specific time within allowed hours
data.description: A time picker lets people choose hours and minutes, and sometimes seconds. Make the 12-hour or 24-hour format clear, define the minute step, and show which times are unavailable.

avoid: Ask for seconds when that precision is not useful
Offer unavailable times and reject them later

lessonPractice.title: A user books a meeting with a New York team. Slots are every 30 minutes and some are full. How can time selection avoid ambiguity?

options.label: Use a 30-minute time picker, disable full slots, and explicitly show the New York time zone
options.feedback: Structured slots control format and availability, while the zone tells users in other regions what instant they selected.

options.label: Use a text field and accept phrases such as tomorrow morning or around three
options.feedback: Natural language cannot map reliably to 30-minute inventory, and tomorrow morning differs across regions.

options.label: Show 09:00 and 09:30 options without saying which region they belong to
options.feedback: The values look precise, but remote users may interpret them in their own local time and book the wrong instant.

data.agentPrompt: Use a 30-minute meeting time picker, disable full and out-of-hours slots, and continuously show America/New_York plus the user's local conversion. Test daylight-saving changes, no availability, and state updates after changing the date.
